source: Mord Hive v0.5, Heroes’ Serious Injury Chart (Roll D66), pp.098-099. Henchmen out of action are instead removed permanently on a D6 of 1-2, otherwise fight the next game as normal (p.099). Ranges from the book expanded to per-roll entries.

table.name: Dead
table.effect: The warrior is dead and his body is abandoned in the dark alleys of Mord Hive, never to be found again. All the weapons and equipment he carried are lost. Remove him from the warband roster.

table.name: Multiple Injuries
table.effect: Roll D6 times on this table. Re-roll any Dead, Captured and further Multiple Injuries results.

table.name: Multiple Injuries
table.effect: Roll D6 times on this table. Re-roll any Dead, Captured and further Multiple Injuries results.

table.name: Leg Wound
table.effect: The warrior’s leg is broken. He suffers a -1 Movement characteristic penalty from now on.

table.name: Arm Wound
table.effect: Roll again: 1 = Severe arm wound, the arm must be amputated and the warrior may only use a single one-handed weapon from now on. 2-6 = Light wound, the warrior must miss the next game.

table.name: Madness
table.effect: Roll a D6. On a 1-3 the warrior suffers from stupidity; on 4-6 the warrior suffers from frenzy from now on.

table.name: Smashed Leg
table.effect: Roll again: 1 = the warrior may not run any more but may still charge. 2-6 = the warrior misses the next game.

table.name: Chest Wound
table.effect: He recovers but is weakened by the injury; his Toughness is reduced by -1.

table.name: Blinded in One Eye
table.effect: The warrior loses an eye: his Ballistic Skill is reduced by -1. If subsequently blinded in his remaining good eye he must retire from the warband.

table.name: Old Battle Wound
table.effect: The warrior survives, but his wound prevents him from fighting if you roll a 1 on a D6 at the start of any battle. Roll at the start of each battle from now on.

table.name: Nervous Condition
table.effect: His Initiative is permanently reduced by -1.

table.name: Hand Injury
table.effect: His Weapon Skill is permanently reduced by -1.

table.name: Deep Wound
table.effect: The warrior has suffered a serious wound and must miss the next D3 games while he recovers. He may do nothing at all while recovering.

table.name: Robbed
table.effect: The warrior manages to escape, but all his weapons, armour and equipment are lost.

table.name: Full Recovery
table.effect: The warrior has been knocked unconscious, or suffers a light wound from which he makes a full recovery.

table.name: Bitter Enmity
table.effect: From now on the warrior hates (roll a D6): 1-3 the individual who caused the injury (if a Henchman, the enemy leader instead); 4 the leader of the warband that caused it; 5 the entire warband responsible; 6 all warbands of that type.

table.name: Captured
table.effect: He may be ransomed at a price set by the captor or exchanged for one of their warband held captive. Captives may be sold to slavers for D6x5 thrones. Chaos or Dark Eldar warbands may kill the captive to gain their leader +1 XP. Ransomed/exchanged captives keep their gear; sold or killed captives leave it with their captors.

table.name: Hardened
table.effect: From now on he is immune to fear.

table.name: Hardened
table.effect: From now on he is immune to fear.

table.name: Horrible Scars
table.effect: The warrior causes fear from now on.

table.name: Sold to the Pits
table.effect: The warrior wakes up in the fighting pits of Mord Hive and must fight a Chrono-Gladiator. Roll for charge and fight as normal. If he loses, roll a D66 of 11-35 to see if he is dead; if not dead he is thrown out without armour and weapons and may rejoin. If he wins he gains 60 thrones, +3 Experience and rejoins with all his gear.

table.name: Survives Against the Odds
table.effect: The warrior survives and rejoins his warband. He gains +2 Experience.
